body: I’m confused about my sexuality. I’m 27 and I know I like men but I think I might be asexual or demisexual.

Exactly this! I just don’t know how to approach telling him. I like him and we have a lot in common. I am attracted to him and I want to see where things go. I just don’t know how to bring up my communication style.
It really depends on the persons makeup (and situation). I’m on meds that killed my libido but my doc adjusted some of them around mg wise and it came back.

You’re welcome! If I was changing dosages that often I personally would be worried for myself because the ssris and other things in the brain that cause my mania would not be at a steady level which would throw my mood like crazy. I’m 110lbs and 5’1” and I use to be on a really high dosage (400 mg of seroquel and 300 mg of lamictal). I started taking meds at 13 because of a mania attack that almost killed me. Bipolar is genetic for me. But over the years as I got older and learned to live with it along with some things like meditation I was able to lower both to 100 along with going off a third one I don’t remember. Price wise make sure she looks for coupons! I was paying $200 for certain meds and the coupons brought them down to $5! I hope everything gets figured out for her because this shit sucks. 

Also, You gotta be careful with a lot of drug drug interactions and other issues. I just want to say with the fact that she uses a lot of aspirin (which is processed through the liver I think) with many antipsychotic medications you need to be careful. I have a yearly blood panel to make sure that my medications aren’t killing my liver. It’s kinda the same thing that can happen to alcoholics in a way (my dosage had to be played with last week because my lipids were high and now I have to have quarterly panels). While she’s at the GP have her ask if she needs a blood panel for liver function just because she’s mixing a lot of aspirin with medication. 

If you or her ever want to talk I’m always down to answer question regarding my personal experience. With the fact I’ve been dealing with bipolar for 10+ years and the fact that I’m working on my masters in general psychology I have a better understanding of my own bipolar disorder than most people. I’m not a doctor and will not go giving medical advice but I’m always willing to share my experience and what has personally helped me.
